title: Ramp recovery & warmback playbook
content:
Purpose
- Scratchpad for debugging repeated capacity thrash during Dedicated GPU pool ramp-ups (what I call warmback: returning GPUs from idle/standby to ready state).
- Capture commands, error snippets, timing, hypotheses and short-lived mitigations. Mostly for my own breadcrumbs and to hand off to SRE if needed.

Incident summary (observed)
- Customer workload experienced queueing and elevated tail latency during traffic spikes between 2026-01-28 09:40 and 2026-01-28 12:10 UTC.
- Autoscaler requested +40 GPUs, cluster reported nodes Ready in k8s quickly but GPU readiness lagged (containers failing to schedule or OOM on init).
- Symptoms: sudden token-generation retries, ~10–30s extra per-request latency, and temporary 5% error rate.

Timeline / notable timestamps
- 2026-01-28 09:39: autoscaler decision: scale up from 60 -> 100 GPUs (policy: p95 latency breach).
- 09:40:7: cloud provider started instances (VM creation logs show successful provisioning by 09:40:37).
- 09:40:47: instances appear in k8s node list (NotReady -> Ready transitions between 09:40:55 and 09:41:20).
- 09:41:25: runtime pods scheduled but fail to pass /internal/pg-init readiness for several seconds.
- 09:41:38: first client retries observed. Warmback window ~18–45s where requests were routed to cold backends and faced longer latency.

Commands tried (local shell snippets)
- Check nodes and gpu plugin status:
  kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
  kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-21 | grep -A6 -i nvidia
  # output: Conditions: Ready True. Kubelet: Runtime not ready for GPU driver until 09:41:10

- Check pod events for runtime init failures:
  kubectl -n rw-serving describe pod rw-runtime-xx-yy | sed -n '1,200p'
  # observed: Warning FailedCreate: mount failed: timeout pulling image after 23s

- Confirm image pull times across nodes (measured):
  for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do echo "NODE $n"; ssh $n 'docker pull registry/redwood/serving-runtime:prod-20260120' ; done
  # average: 6s on prewarmed nodes, 22s on cold nodes (network + registry throttling suspected)

Error snippets (copied raw)
- kubelet: "nvidia-container-runtime: timeout waiting for device plugin to register"
- pod event: "Back-off pulling image \"registry/redwood/serving-runtime:prod-20260120\""
- runtime logs: "failed to restore kv-cache: file not found; falling back to cold-load"
- autoscaler log: "scale-up observed, but warm-signal not seen within 30s; marking pool as partially-warmed"

Observed metrics (sample)
- GPU init latency distribution during event: median 12s, p95 38s, max 74s (n=42 new GPUs).
- Docker/image pull time correlated strongly with region/availability-zone.
- Container start failures: 3/42 initial pods OOM'd during model load stage (insufficient reserved host memory on those nodes).

Hypotheses (prioritized)
1) Image pull & container init dominate warmback latency. Cold nodes pay large image-pull penalty; repeated on spikes causes autoscaler to oscillate.
2) GPU driver/device-plugin registration race with kubelet => pod becomes unschedulable until device-plugin reports. This yields a silent 10–30s gap.
3) Insufficient host-level reserved memory leads to model loader OOMs on some instance types when multiple workloads kick off simultaneously.
4) Autoscaler warm-signal relies on a single readiness probe path that can be transiently false during model warm steps, so scaling decision loops because readiness seen too late.
5) Registry/network throttling: bursts on cold starts amplify pull times.

Mitigations attempted (quick & reversible)
- Short-term (during incident): manual pinned routing to larger, already-warmed pool (dedicated-large-a) for 25m to avoid thrash. Reduced errors but increased cost.
- Increased image pull concurrency limit on registry for our org (tuned at 2026-01-28 10:03) — measured slight improvement.
- Bumped node-reserved memory from 2Gi -> 4Gi on suspicious instance types to reduce OOMs (applied in a canary AZ).

Playbook steps to reproduce locally
- Simulate cold pool: drain node set and delete runtime images, then trigger scale-up with 20 simultaneous requests using load-generator (loadgen/ab-like script).
- Observe timings for: VM provisioning (cloud console), k8s node Ready, device-plugin registration, image pull, model load, readiness probe.

Diagnostics to collect on next incident (automate these):
- Timestamped node events (kubelet/device-plugin logs) correlated with autoscaler decisions.
- Per-node image-pull duration histogram (via node-exporter + custom metric).
- Runtime pod lifecycle trace: schedule -> pulled -> started -> readiness.
- Kernel/dmesg for GPU-driver errors.
- Model loader memory max RSS sample during cold load.

Longer-term remediation ideas (ranked)
A) Pre-pull images on newly created nodes (init daemonset/prefetch job) so image pull penalty reduced to ~0–3s.
B) Introduce a lightweight warm-signal endpoint: node-level agent marks GPU 'ready-for-serving' only after driver + device-plugin + image prefetch + model cache warm (can be conservative). Autoscaler should consider both node Ready and warm-signal.
C) Stagger model loading across pods on the same node (random jitter before heavy model init) to avoid host memory pressure.
D) Cache model KV on a shared NVM store on node to shorten model cold-load time and avoid simultaneous OOMs.
E) Autoscaler backoff tweak: only remove capacity if pool has been warm for >5m; suppress oscillation during rapid bursts.

Experiment notes (what to try next)
- Canary A: enable image prefetch on 4 nodes in us-west-2a for 48h and measure GPU init p95.
- Canary B: implement a tiny warm-signal in runtime (responds true only after model cache loaded or after a short 3s post-scheduler success) and have autoscaler read it for a subset of pools.
- Canary C: reduce parallelism of model loader by adding 300–700ms startup jitter in the runtime entrypoint when env DEBUG_WARM_JITTER=true.

Immediate next actions (for handoff)
- Create an alert that captures: when autoscaler requested >10 GPUs and median GPU init > 15s for that scale op (INF-INC-2026-01).
- Spin up one canary cluster with prefetch daemonset; collect 72h of metrics. (owner: Jasper)
- Put a temporary routing rule to prefer already-warmed pools when available (owner: Anika).

Notes to myself
- Keep this file as the running journal. Paste interesting outputs here in full when I have them.
- If SRE asks for a replay, I have the exact sequence and the loadgen config in the linked GH gist (link: https://gist.github.com/maya-p/ramp-replay).

Scratch: common commands to copy-paste
- autoscaler logs (since time): gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="redwood-dedicated" AND textPayload:autoscaler' --start="2026-01-28T09:35:00Z" --limit=500
- collect node kubelet logs: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-$n --tail=500 > /tmp/$n-kubelet.log; done

End of entry (2026-02-20).
